## Project Description

This experiment examines how exposure to concentrations of microplastics
relevant to end-of-century predictions affects the thermal tolerance
(CTmax), acclimation capacity, and metabolic rate of Skistodiaptomus
pallidus under ambient and elevated temperature conditions relevant to
end-of-century heatwave predictions. The CTmax of four treatment groups
will be compared at the end of a 7 day treatment period, with each group
having either no MPs or MPs present and having either control
temperatures (16C) or heatwave temperatures (22C). Results will improve
our understanding of how multiple stressors interact to shape copepod
resilience in a warming, plastic-polluted world.

## Questions, Objectives, Hypotheses

Questions: 1. How does exposure to end-of-century concentrations of MPs
affect the thermal tolerance of S. pallidus? 2. Do MPs affect S.
pallidus's ability to acclimate to end-of-century heatwave temperatures?
3. Does exposure to MPs affect the metabolic rate of S. pallidus?

Hypotheses: 1. Exposure to end-of-century concentrations of MPs will
cause an increase in thermal limits because of stress pathways activated
by the MPs being similar to thermal resistance stress pathways. 2. MPs
will increase S. pallidus's acclimation ability to end-of-century
heatwave temperatures. 3. Exposure to MPs will increase the metabolic
rate of S. pallidus to help cope with the stress.

## Study Design

This section should provide a detailed description of the study design.
In addition to protocols and methodological details, this section should
include a detailed accounting of replication and sample sizes.

Species: Skistodiaptomus pallidus #Species Generation: F\>3 Temperature
Treatments: 16C (Control), 22C (Warm) MP Treatments: None, Present Trait
Measurement: CTmax Population: Centennial park\
Replicates: 3 Animals/dish = 40 Total animals needed = 100 (x/replicate)

1.  Animals are collected from field and brought to lab.
2.  On setup day X adult females are selected from the lab culture and
    are evenly split into four different dishes with XmL of DIO and
    \~0.5mL-1.5mL C. ozolini.
3.  By the end of setup there will be four dishes: N+C, N+W, MP+C, MP+W,
    and each dish will have X animals. Equation used to get \#
    animals/dish: Animals/dish = ((# of assays \* \# of tubes)/# of
    dishes) + (0.5 \* \# of assays)
4.  Dishes are given their respective amounts of MPs.
5.  Each dish is placed into their respective incubators, a temperature
    sensor is also placed in the incubators in a dish with 150mL of tap
    water to closely monitor the internal temperatures of the incubators
    (in the incubator there are two shelves, the temperature treatments
    are always on the same shelf as one another but alternate every
    replicate, also the incubator that is used as the control or the
    warm alternates every replicate).
6.  On day 7, 4 CTmax assays are ran using 2-3 animals from each dish in
    each assay. Tube placements for each assay are randomized using
    Skisto_LARA/Scripts/00_tube_assignments.R
7.  This is replicated 3 times.

## Statistics

### Data Processing

Data is processed in the controller script: - Pop = "thermometer" is
filtered out - CTmax values \< 34.5 are filtered out - acc_hours is
defined - datetime is mutated to fit our date and time format

### Key Summary Statistics

| Summary Statistic | Calculated For Which Groups |
|----|----|
| Mean +/- Standard Error | CTmax for each treatment: N+C, N+W, M P+C, MP+W. CTmax for each treatment + thermal tolerance, how it changes over the course of the experiment, how the mean of rate of acclimation is a cross treatments |

### Statistical Tests of Hypotheses

Hypothesis 1: - Tests of assumptions:

-   How model fit will be evaluated: Using the performance package in R

-   Post-hoc tests: Comparisons of mean CTmax will be conducted between
    MP-present and MP-absent treatments within each acclimation
    temperature (i.e., N+C vs. MP+C; N+W vs. MP+W).

-   Caveats/Caution when interpreting results: Moving animals between
    dishes/tubes on setup day and assay day could stress them slightly,
    which may lower or raise their measured CTmax independent of MP
    exposure. (Not likely)

-   Handling missing values: Missing values will be excluded from
    analysis, this hypothesis relies on comparisons across the
    acclimation period.

    Notes: Simplify: To refine we are missing the middle, what are we
    using to do this

    Post-hoc test (after the fact test): Is there a significant
    difference between treatments (group means), Slops (acclimation)

-   Hypothesis 2:

    -   Tests of assumptions:

    -   How model fit will be evaluated: Using the performance package
        in R

    -   Post-hoc tests: Comparing the change in CTmax across the
        acclimation period between MP-present and MP-absent animals
        within the warm (22°C) treatment (i.e., N+W vs. MP+W)

    -   Caveats/Caution when interpreting results: Moving animals
        between dishes/tubes on setup day and assay day could stress
        them slightly, which may lower or raise their measured CTmax
        independent of MP exposure.

    -   Handling missing values: Missing values will be excluded from
        analysis, this hypothesis relies on comparisons across the
        acclimation period.
